scope: Proposition 4.6 (Uniform boundary conditional averaging) of the manuscript “Conformal universality of bulk Ising correlations under weak interactions” (preprints/Conformal-universality-of-bulk-Ising-correlations-under-weak-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8a815e7845436e07), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix support and separation factors, including a constant C0. There are C < ∞ and ℓ0 < ∞ such that the following holds. For each fixed ℓ = R/s ≥ ℓ0, there are a lower threshold for s, a sufficiently large chart-window factor, and a sufficiently small flatness threshold, all allowed to depend on ℓ but not on the boundary orientation. Suppose a physical boundary point lies within C0s of the common center of the support and cutting squares, and that throughout the chart window the boundary is a single C1 graph with slope deviation from its tangent below that threshold. Retain its homogeneous nearest-neighbor boundary type in the conditional averaging. Then, for every bounded F supported in the inner square, inf c∈R ∥PRF − c∥∞ ≤ C(s/R)2 ∥F∥∞ (4.17) in fixed boundary conditions. The same holds for even F in free boundary conditions. For complex F, take c ∈ C and adjust the constant harmlessly.
